Read-only requests to the dataset's Socrata API on NYC Open Data (https://data.cityofnewyork.us/resource/dg92-zbpx.json) at the moment you ask, with an app token when SOCRATA_APP_TOKEN is set. Each tool sends one query, such as a keyword search, an agency name, a notice type or a date range, and returns the newest matching notices.

dataset.scopeNote: Known gap: Most notices in the dataset have no notice type (about 88% when checked on 2026-11-13). get_notices_by_type, get_procurement_notices, get_public_hearings and get_open_solicitations select by notice type, so they never return those notices; search_notices, get_notices_by_agency and get_notices_by_date_range do. Known gap: Before 2013 the dataset holds far fewer notices a year: about 3,500 to 5,500, against 70,000 to 110,000 a year from 2014 on, when checked on 2026-11-13. Caveat: Each tool returns at most 100 notices (200 for a date range), newest first (open solicitations: soonest deadline first), so a long list is cut short at that limit. Caveat: An empty answer means no notice in the dataset matched the query, not that no such notice was published. Check City Record Online or the printed City Record before relying on it.
